messages:
simon: heads-up — nightly perf job flagged a p95 regression after the merge of PR #6789 (scheduler + prefetch refactor). CI shows ~+25% p95 on decode. attaching CI summary: https://ci.internal/perf/3141592653 :eyes:
ci-bot: perf/nightly-decode FAILED: p95 increased 24.7% vs baseline (threshold 10%). job id 3141592653-verify
maria: saw the same on canary-3, tails look noisy starting at ~09:12. shortseq traffic shows the largest delta. flamegraph attached (s3://perf/3141592653/flame.svg)
raj: quick profiler dump from canary:
```
top stacks by cpu% (sampled):
 - Runtime::DecodePath::process_tokens 38%
 - KVPrefetchScheduler::dispatch 26%
 - Batcher::emit_batch 12%
 - attention_kernel::apply 9%
```
heap traces show spikes in prefetch queue length leading to backpressure on the fused-batcher. suspect the new adaptive prefetch heuristic is deferring prefetch while batcher queue is 'near full' causing uneven latencies.
elaine: oncall noticed pod burst restarts around the same time (OOM kill on canary-3) — could be memory amplification from queued prefetch buffers. logs: `kubelet: evicting pod, memory_pressure`
simon: can we bisect to the exact commit? PR #6789 had two commits: 9a1f2 (prefetch scheduler) and b3cde (metrics). I'll try a quick git-bisect against the perf job on a local repro branch.
anna: @simon FYI I kicked off a gated canary run with the last-known-good (before 9a1f2) and an engineered tiny traffic replay. will post results in ~20m.
raj: did a quick local delta: reverting 9a1f2 reduces p95 back to baseline in my microbench (shortseq synth). patch diff summary:
```
- KVPrefetchScheduler.defer_when_queue_near_full = true
+ KVPrefetchScheduler.defer_when_queue_near_full = false
```
so the heuristic was too aggressive for short sequences — it starves the KV warmup path.
maria: thanks. while we decide rollback, can we add a temporary guard to cap prefetch buffer memory and avoid OOM? small kube resource bump won't help the tail.
simon: agreed. propose immediate action: (1) revert commit 9a1f2 in canary -> observe, (2) hotfix to cap prefetch buffers to 4 per-connection and backpressure metrics, (3) follow-up proper fix to make defer heuristic sequence-length-aware.
devops-bot: deploy pipeline started: revert-9a1f2 -> canary-3. build 3141592701.
ci-bot: perf/canary-compare started for build 3141592701.
anna: canary results: p95 back to baseline (within noise) after revert. no OOMs observed in the window.
raj: landed temporary hotfix PR that caps per-conn prefetch buffers and exposes metric `prefetch.buffer_count` for alerts. PR #6795.
maria: rolling the hotfix to staging now. also added a shortseq regression test to the perf harness to catch this pattern.
simon: reverting 9a1f2 in main and applying hotfix. will post revert PR and link.
ci-bot: revert PR merged (PR #6790). hotfix PR merged (PR #6795).
elaine: raising incident postmortem draft to doc the root cause and follow-ups: make prefetch heuristic aware of sequence-length distribution, add mem caps, add perf gate for shortseq p95.
raj: follow-ups: (a) rework heuristic to use per-model shortseq ratio, (b) add unit test for prefetch/backpressure interplay, (c) run a 24h stress with mixed seq distribution. assigning to @raj and @maria.
simon: thanks all — good triage. closing thread once postmortem linked. :thumbsup:
